latest_messages.headline: Labor Day — markets closed. Homework done for Tuesday: Nordson (NDSN) is the one clean new idea.
latest_messages.body: No trading today (Labor Day holiday) — research only. The dominant theme is interest rates: a hot jobs report has a Fed rate HIKE genuinely on the table for Sept 16, and two inflation reports this week (Thu + the big one Fri) will set the mood. When rates rise, pricey tech gets hit hardest, so I'm favoring steadier 'rate-insensitive' names. One cleared all my quality checks: Nordson (NDSN), an industrial-equipment maker with a beat-and-raise and two recent Wall Street target hikes. Tuesday I'll consider a ~$10k starter only if it opens at a clean price (funded by trimming our S&P 500 sleeve); if it gaps or the tape is jumpy before Friday's inflation print, I wait. Both stocks (JPM +8.8%, ATI +0.5%) healthy and protected. Cash ~$19.8k (~20%), about $9.8k above my ~$10k target, ready to redeploy.

latest_messages.headline: Week ending 2026-09-04: −0.61% | SPY +0.12% | alpha −0.73% | grade C−
latest_messages.body: A losing week, and the whole story is one avoidable trade. Good news: I fixed last week's demerit — put our idle cash to work on Monday as planned. But I then handed nearly the entire week's loss to Synopsys, which I bought the day before a hot jobs report; it's a rate-sensitive stock and got 7%-stopped the next morning (−$708). No company bad news — a timing mistake, and the 2nd time this exact pattern has bitten me. I broadened my own written caution against buying jumpy, rate-sensitive stocks right before big economic reports, and put it on notice: a 3rd time makes it a hard rule. No safety rule was loosened — the 7% stop and quality bar both worked. Cumulative vs the market is now ~−2% (run-worst). Cash ~$19.8k held over the long weekend; Fed meeting Sept 16 keeps me cautious.
